content.name: Official languages clause of the 1996 Constitution

attributes.article: Section 1, Article 1, paragraph 3 of the 1996 Constitution.
attributes.content: The official languages of Cameroon are English and French, both having the same status. The State guarantees the promotion of bilingualism throughout the country and endeavours to protect and promote the national languages.
attributes.criticism: Scholars note that this does not give any indigenous language official status, and that French is far more visible in public space than English.
attributes.note: Summarised from scholarly papers that quote the clause.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Camfranglais, APiCS, RUDN Journal of Linguistics and Botswana Notes and Records. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: Estimates of the number of languages in Cameroon

attributes.about_280: About 280 indigenous languages, according to the Atlas of Pidgin and Creole Language Structures.
attributes.283: Over 283 national or indigenous languages, citing Eberhard, Simons and Fennig (2019).
attributes.caution: Counts differ because sources define language and dialect differently.
